# Plan and Implement

## Change Summary

Implemented the pending remediation around the canonical chemistry helper layer. Added a cached `ConcentrationView` API on `WaterState` plus `TankState::concentrations()` so multi-helper call sites reuse one net-water-volume lookup, then switched hot consumers such as snapshots, shrimp stress/stability, and threshold events onto that path. Refactored `nitrogen_cycle`, `algae_growth`, and `plant_growth` to read canonical concentration helpers instead of raw dissolved totals; to preserve existing tuning while removing tank-size dependence, legacy half-saturation fields are now normalized through a 20 L reference-volume compatibility conversion. Restored schema-2 save compatibility by migrating legacy dissolved totals from gross volume to canonical net volume inside `SaveFile::from_json`, and updated the API load handler to use that migration path. Also documented the legacy-compat parameter semantics and the `soft_acidic` preset rationale, expanded regression coverage for the new behavior, and derived `Default` for `StartupOverrides` to clear the pre-existing clippy warning.

## Steps

0. [Completed] Audited the pending amendments and related history to separate actual code gaps from already-isolated prior behavior changes, then mapped the required fixes across core types, systems, saves, API handling, docs, and tests.
1. [Completed] Added `ConcentrationView` and `TankState::concentrations()`, and refactored multi-helper consumers such as snapshots, events, and shrimp systems to reuse one canonical net-volume lookup instead of recomputing substrate depth for every helper call.
2. [Completed] Updated nitrogen-cycle, algae, and plant limitation math to consume canonical concentration helpers, using a 20 L reference-volume compatibility conversion for legacy half-saturation fields so identical water-column concentrations no longer get different Monod factors solely because tank volume changed.
3. [Completed] Restored schema-2 save compatibility by migrating legacy dissolved totals from gross to net volume in `SaveFile::from_json`, routed API loads through that migration path, documented the legacy-compat parameter semantics and `soft_acidic` preset rationale, and accepted the clippy-driven `StartupOverrides` `Default` derive cleanup.
4. [Completed] Expanded regression coverage for concentration-view equivalence, schema-2 migration, decomposer/plant/algae volume invariance, and updated nutrient-pressure scenario assertions, then ran formatting, targeted tests, full workspace tests, and clippy.

## Validation Evidence

- `cargo fmt --all` completed successfully.
- `cargo test -q -p tank_core --test concentration_helpers` passed with 9 tests, including the new concentration-view equivalence regression.
- `cargo test -q -p tank_core --test save_load` passed with 5 tests, including schema-2 gross-to-net migration coverage.
- `cargo test -q -p tank_core --test cycling` passed with 9 tests, including the new decomposer concentration-invariance regression.
- `cargo test -q -p tank_core --test plant_algae_integration` passed with 6 tests, including new plant/algae volume-invariance coverage.
- `cargo test -q -p tank_core --test end_to_end` passed with 17 tests after retuning the legacy half-saturation compatibility conversion around the 20 L reference volume.
- `cargo test --quiet` completed successfully across the workspace.
- `cargo clippy --all-targets --quiet` completed successfully; the pre-existing `StartupOverrides` `derivable_impls` warning is no longer present.

## Outstanding Risks

- Legacy process field ids such as `aob_k_tan_mg` and `plant_half_saturation_n_mg_total` still need formal rename work across presets/saves/docs; the runtime semantics are now concentration-based, but the persisted names can still mislead future contributors.
- Plant nutrient limitation still blends water-column concentration factors with substrate-total accessibility factors; full root-zone / areal normalization remains deferred to the downstream habitat-normalization work.
- Schema-2 migration assumes legacy saves were authored with gross-volume-scaled dissolved totals; a hand-edited or previously pre-migrated schema-2 file would be rescaled again on load.
